_note: Operator-owned definitions for `manage.py register_products`. Data only: no plan, no price and no credential is defined here (those are commercial decisions made in the Super Admin console). Each product's trial (enabled, 7 days: the owner's decision of 2026-10-11) is applied only when the product has no trial configuration yet, and a trial starts only on a published plan staff mark eligible. Descriptions and features are DRAFT copy to be confirmed by each product's owner and editable in the product manager. Each redirect URI is the path a product's OIDC client (authorization code + PKCE, private_key_jwt) must serve; all four products implement exactly these (2026-10-12). Single sign-on works once an operator runs `manage.py connect_product_sso` with the product's public key (it sets the redirect URIs and scopes, registers the credential and activates the integration). Until an unrevoked credential exists the console reports 'SSO integration required'. `sign_in_mode` (ADR-044) declares how each product lets people in: EasyBook and Easy CRM are `sso_only` because their production deployments run with WORKEASY360_SSO_ONLY on (the owner's decision of 2026-10-12) - switch one to `sso_optional`, with its `login_url`, in the console if its deployment re-enables its own password sign-in. Easy Project and Easy Help Desk implement the same client (2026-10-12: repositories Project-Module and helpdesk-workeasy, each with docs/workeasy360-sso.md) and are `sso_only` too: Easy Project never had a sign-in of its own, and the Help Desk's production deployment runs with WORKEASY360_SSO_ONLY on. An environment that registered either before then holds it `local_only`; `connect_product_sso` switches it to `sso_only` when it registers the key. `post_logout_redirect_uris` are where Workeasy360 may return a browser after the product's 'sign out of Workeasy360 too'. A product registered before ADR-044 reads as `sso_only`.
